releaseNotes: Expanded onboarding into typed ONB-00 through ONB-22 catalog nodes so the durable engine can schedule, fan out, join, checkpoint, retry, resume, and verify the complete consumer onboarding system rather than executing one coarse prose node.

Rebuilt product/ONBOARDING.md as the canonical evidence, first-value, state, identity, analytics, design, monetization, lifecycle, implementation, hard-cutover, and zero-legacy contract, with a faithful searchable generated HTML view.

Added check:onboarding-graph to both package layouts and the standard audit, with deterministic fixtures for review timing, deferrals, placeholder completion, typed screen and control contracts, and legacy removal. Updated app-agent roles to continue the graph through Compound Engineering implementation and final proof.

CI review pass: fixed a ReferenceError in check-onboarding-graph.ts where TEMPLATE_DIRECTIVE_VERBS was declared after tablePlaceholderCells() could already be called from top-level script code (moved the const above its first use), applied Prettier formatting, and added the missing docs/plans/attachments/2026-08-port-ledger.md row (plus rebased onto origin/main, which had advanced with unrelated merges since this branch was cut).

Fixed three interlocking bugs in tablePlaceholderCells() that a full local audit run surfaced once the TDZ crash above stopped masking them. 'done' was in the bare generic-completion-word blocklist, so the Graph Run table's own correct terminal status value made check:onboarding-graph reject every real completed onboarding lane -- removed it (graphRunNodeDone() already requires it literally, so it needs no separate placeholder check). The repeated-cell heuristic keyed on first-word-only, so a genuinely filled Evidence Ledger with many distinct 'Evidence-N: ...' rows tripped it purely because they share a label prefix -- switched to whole-cell-text repetition, which still catches an actually-unfilled table (identical text repeated) without false-positiving on distinct content. onboarding.fixtures.ts's own fillTemplateDirectiveCells() only replaced cells starting with literally 'Record', leaving the shipped template's other directive-verb cells ('Define', 'Choose', etc.) unfilled, so its 'completed' fixture was never actually complete -- broadened it to mirror the validator's own TEMPLATE_DIRECTIVE_VERBS set (then hit and fixed the identical before-first-use TDZ ordering bug in that same fixture file). Also corrected the port ledger's grand-total row: my own counting script had matched the summary table's own header row as if it were a data row, overstating every bucket by one.

Closed the review round on the full onboarding graph: ONB-22's catalog gate now runs check-onboarding-graph.ts --require-done, a new wrapper that rejects the shipped template (lane still not_started) while leaving the general audit's lenient check:onboarding-graph untouched -- registered the wrapper as a deliberate audit-plan exclusion so catalog validation and package-parity both accept it, and added fixtures proving both the reject and a genuinely-completed accept. ONB-18 now depends on the real Design Room workflow instead of only narrating a high-fidelity prototype in its own Markdown packet, so the engine cannot unblock ONB-20 on prose alone. Re-verified against ground truth (not assumption) that the regex, catalog-encoding, Copy-column, deferred-lane, and placeholder-detection review threads were already fixed by earlier commits on this branch, and re-ran the full launchbench and catalog fixture suites to confirm. Aligned the review-prompt timing doctrine (earn eligibility at first value, request later outside first-run onboarding) across emotional-design-system.md, consumer-product-design-agency.md, influencer-sponsorship-engine.md, and launchbench-evals.md's own failure-mode index, which still described the pre-onboarding-conversion.md timing after push-notification-lifecycle.md was already fixed.

A second review round found six more real gaps behind --require-done's own logic, not just doctrine drift. ONB-22 was classified actionClass 'mutate', letting the durable engine execute its hard cutover and legacy deletion under an ordinary experience-domain grant instead of the autonomy engine's protected destructive waiver path -- reclassified it 'destructive' with a founderOnlyActions entry. The not_needed/deferred skip exempted --require-done too, so a deferred workspace passed ONB-22's own strict gate without ever finishing onboarding -- the skip now applies only to the general (non-strict) invocation. The strict block checked every ONB node's Graph Run table entry and every table cell's placeholder state but never the Verification section's own '- [ ] ...' checklist, so a fixture leaving all eleven final checks unchecked still passed --require-done -- added a dedicated unchecked-item count. graphRunNodeDone() searched every cell in a Graph Run row for the literal word 'done' instead of reading the Status column specifically, so a 'partial' row mentioning 'done' in its owner or result prose was wrongly accepted -- it now locates the Status column by the table's own header before reading it. tablePlaceholderCells()'s generic completion-word blocklist rejected legitimate prescribed terminal answers ('Yes', 'Pass', 'N/A', ...) that the template itself asks for in the Effort-Before-Value, policy, and Prototype And Design Proof matrices -- removed the blocklist, keeping only the literal word 'placeholder', the directive-verb first-word check, and the whole-cell repetition heuristic. And product/onboarding.html's decoded raw-source view carried internal vocabulary (lane, gate, artifact, not_started, ...) into the browser-visible DOM behind a static <script>/<pre> pair that check-founder-copy.ts's script-stripping scan could never see regardless of surrounding markup -- moved the source view into the repo's sanctioned <details>'Technical details' disclosure (the same pattern render-launch-cockpit.ts and render-design-room.ts already use) and taught check-founder-copy.ts to decode base64 script payloads and scan them too, exempting only the ones whose target element actually sits inside that disclosure. Verified the founder-copy fix by reverting the HTML locally and confirming the gate now genuinely fails the leak, not just structurally happens to pass.

A third review round found the remaining table-only blind spot: tablePlaceholderCells() and graphRunNodeDone() only ever looked at table rows, so the Execution Mode section's own directive-verb-led paragraph ('Record `greenfield`, ...') and seven similar prose sections stayed exactly as the shipped template wrote them under --require-done, and the artifact's own top-of-document 'Status: `word`' header was never cross-checked against the done lane it was claiming. Added proseDirectiveLines() (same TEMPLATE_DIRECTIVE_VERBS first-word check as the table version, folded into the existing onboarding_graph.placeholder_complete error) and a dedicated onboarding_graph.artifact_status_not_done check requiring the header to read exactly done. The fixture-side prose filler swaps only each directive line's leading verb for a word outside TEMPLATE_DIRECTIVE_VERBS_PATTERN rather than replacing the whole line, because several of these same sentences (e.g. the First Value And Activation paragraph) are also where requirePhrases() finds its required doctrine phrases -- a whole-line replacement would have silently broken those checks instead of fixing this one.

A fourth review round found the placeholder-detection heuristics were still gameable rather than content-checking. tablePlaceholderCells()'s whole-cell repetition check missed boilerplate that varies only by an embedded counter (e.g. 'Evidence-1: source-backed implementation detail dated 2026-08-08', 'Evidence-2: ...'), which is exactly the shape of the fixture's own former filler and, per a direct count against the shipped template, would also have let a real launch fill 84 of 138 directive cells with a single copy-pasted sentence -- added a digit-normalized repetition count (digits collapsed to '#') alongside the exact-text one, so counter-varying filler is caught without rejecting genuinely distinct rows. proseDirectiveLines() was, in the same round, found to over-flag: two fixed doctrine sentences (Analytics Contract's 'Define a machine-readable schema...' and First Value And Activation's 'Define First value rendered...') sit directly above their own capture table and carry required doctrine phrases verbatim, so a genuinely complete artifact that correctly left them untouched would have failed -- scoped the check to only flag a directive-verb-led line when its own section (down to the next heading) has no table. And the not_needed/deferred skip accepted a bare status with no explanation, since check-lane-coverage.ts already treats nonempty evidence as sufficient rationale for a skip even though evidence answers 'did the lane produce anything' rather than 'why is it not happening' -- added onboarding_graph.deferred_without_reason, requiring a recorded blocker or reason before the exemption applies. Rewrote the fixture's own fillTemplateDirectiveCells() to derive each filled cell's text from its own row's identifying content and column header instead of an incrementing counter, so the 'genuinely completed' fixture states remain immune to the new normalized-repetition check while staying a faithful test of real validator behavior; added dedicated fixtures proving the counter-boilerplate rejection, the fixed-doctrine-prose exemption, and the deferred-without-reason rejection.

A fifth review round found two engine-wiring defects rather than validator logic gaps. runDeterministicGates() (core/session/run.ts) invokes every gate via `npm run --prefix <skillRoot> <gate>`, and npm's own documented --prefix behavior executes the underlying script with the package root as process.cwd() regardless of the caller's actual working directory -- confirmed empirically with a standalone reproduction. The engine already set BUSINESS_ROOT in the child's env for exactly this reason, but parseCliArgs() (tooling/lib/launch-state.ts, shared by 43+ business validators) never read it, defaulting root to process.cwd() unconditionally -- so ONB-22's gate, and every other durable-engine-invoked deterministic gate, resolved the skill package instead of the business workspace and could never pass even on a genuinely completed launch. Fixed by defaulting root to BUSINESS_ROOT when set, before an explicit --root flag (still checked afterward) can override it for direct CLI use; verified by reproducing the exact npm run --prefix invocation with and without BUSINESS_ROOT, confirming it now correctly resolves the workspace. Separately, ONB-03 through ONB-08 -- the six research nodes evidence-joined by ONB-09 -- were domain.experience with no gate command, which compilePlan() compiles to verification 'none': an empty or fabricated research packet could unlock ONB-09 and the later destructive cutover with no check at all. Reassigned all six to domain.research, matching the existing workflow.research.* convention (domainId drives compilePlan()'s JUDGMENT_DOMAINS fresh-context routing; areaIds stays area.product-experience), so each now requires fresh-context judgment verification before being accepted.

A sixth review round found the round-5 domain.research reassignment itself was wrong in production: core/session/run.ts's acceptVerification() -- the only thing that can promote a reconciled-but-blocked node to succeeded -- is called from exactly one site, inside the deterministic-gate branch; fresh_context acceptance has no production caller anywhere, only test fixtures (verification/fixtures/engine.fixtures.ts), so ONB-03 through ONB-08 would have stayed permanently blocked in a real run, and the domain reassignment also silently dropped them out of an experience-scoped session brief's dispatch scope (scopeHints: ['domain.experience']). Reverted all six nodes to domain.experience and instead gave each an explicit deterministic gate (check:onboarding-evidence-onb-03 through -08, added to both package.json layouts, registered as deliberate audit-plan and launchbench exclusions since each checks a specific node's own mid-run output packet that does not exist against the shipped, never-executed template) via a new validation/business/experience/check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts, which rejects a missing, stub-length (<400 non-fence characters), still-templated (TODO/TBD/PLACEHOLDER/not_started), or prose-free packet -- the same structural-only limitation as every other deterministic gate in this system, since judging whether research is actually true still has no production verifier. This is the more robust fix: deterministic gates have a working production acceptance path, so it closes the original round-5 gap (verification 'none') without reintroducing either of round 6's regressions. Caught a self-inflicted bug during fixture verification: the new fixture helper's `'text' + topic + '. '.repeat(15)` only repeated the trailing '. ', not the full sentence, so the 'passing' fixture was actually testing a 179-character stub and failed its own assertion -- fixed by building the full sentence first, then repeating it.

The same round also flagged ONB-20 (adversarial QA): domain.experience with no gate compiled to verification 'none', so an empty ONB-20-adversarial-qa.md could unlock ONB-21 and the destructive ONB-22 cutover with no policy, instrumentation, accessibility, or provider QA behind it. Fixed with the same pattern as ONB-03..08 -- gates: ['check:onboarding-evidence-onb-20'] reusing the same check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts validator, registered as the same audit-plan exclusion, with fixtures proving the missing- and passing-packet cases.

A seventh review round found four more real gaps. ONB-22 was idempotent: true, but detectOrphans() (core/engine/runstate.ts) hands an idempotent node's orphaned attempt straight back to 'ready' for blind re-dispatch -- safe for a retryable content mutation, not for a node that applies a one-time provider/runtime transformation and deletes legacy architecture, where a lost heartbeat could mean the destructive work partially landed already. Set idempotent: false so an orphaned ONB-22 attempt instead routes to needs_readback and waits for a provider read-back to establish ground truth. Separately, ONB-22's own gate (check:onboarding-graph-complete) reads only product/ONBOARDING.md and project state, so it could accept a run that left product/onboarding.html missing or stale; added check:generated-pages -- the existing mechanism that byte-matches every authored-from page against a fresh render of its Markdown source -- to ONB-22's gates. That surfaced a real production bug in the process: check-generated-pages.ts computed its own business-root default independently of parseCliArgs (tooling/lib/launch-state.ts) instead of reusing it, so it never read BUSINESS_ROOT, and its skill-relative fallback path did not even exist -- masked until now because run-audit.ts's rootArgs always passed an explicit --root. Fixed by honoring BUSINESS_ROOT first (matching the round-5 parseCliArgs fix) and correcting the broken fallback to point at workspace/business, the same template templatesRoot() already uses; verified all three resolution paths (BUSINESS_ROOT env, explicit --root, and the corrected default) independently. Finally, knowledge/process/artifact-contracts.md still described the pre-onboarding-conversion.md App Review popup timing ('immediately after the first value/value-reveal screen') in three places, missed from the earlier doctrine-alignment sweep -- corrected to the canonical earn-eligibility-then-request-later-outside-onboarding wording from onboarding-conversion.md:94 -- and its product/onboarding.html section claimed the page was 'the visual proof for onboarding and paywall flow' requiring mobile-dimension screens and mascot states, which conflicts with the page's actual shipped implementation (a rendered execution-record document with a collapsed source disclosure, per tooling/lib/artifact-pages.ts's renderSourceArtifactPage) -- rewrote the section to describe the page's real role and point onboarding's visual-proof requirement at design/design.html (fulfilled by the Design Room), which already carries it.

An eighth review round found three more production-correctness gaps. First, ONB-22's gate (check-onboarding-graph.ts) read lanes.onboarding only from state/PROJECT_STATE.yaml (v1), but core/session/run.ts's resolveWorkspacePaths() treats state/business-state.json (v2) as a durable-engine-managed workspace's canonical state, which may have no PROJECT_STATE.yaml at all -- so ONB-22 could report the lane permanently missing on a genuinely completed v2 run. Rather than a repo-wide v1/v2 bridge (the validator suite's other ~27 loadProjectState() callers touch v2 sections -- project, narrative, autonomy, continuity, control-plane -- with no verified 1:1 v1 shape, where a wrong silent mapping would be worse than the current clear error), added loadLaneFromBusinessStateV2() to tooling/lib/launch-state.ts, scoped to exactly the one field this gate needs, with an inverse status map that core/schema/migrate-v1.ts's migrateLaneStatus() guarantees is total for a lane's six possible values; error messages now cite whichever state file actually supplied the data. Second, ONB-21 (Compound Engineering plan) had no gate and domain.experience isn't a JUDGMENT_DOMAINS entry, so compilePlan() assigned verification 'none' and an executor could return its declared artifact ID with no real plan behind it, unblocking the destructive ONB-22 cutover -- fixed with the same check-onboarding-evidence-packet.ts pattern as ONB-03..08/ONB-20. Third, a domain.experience-scoped session could never dispatch the onboarding graph at all: ONB-00 depends on workflow.data.analytics-and-attribution-blueprint (domain.data), and core/session/run.ts's dispatch loop only ever filtered the CURRENT ready frontier by scope, silently breaking with no explanation when scoping emptied it -- never expanding into the dependency closure to find why. Expanding the closure to auto-dispatch out-of-scope work was rejected as an authorization-boundary risk (a scoped session must never silently run work outside its founder-granted scope); instead added findOutOfScopeBlockers(), which walks only not-yet-succeeded in-scope nodes' dependency chains to name the actual blocker without touching dispatch. The first implementation flagged the wrong cases -- any out-of-scope ready node, not just an actual blocker for in-scope work -- which broke an existing fixture asserting that unrelated out-of-scope ready work is correctly left silent; corrected before shipping, and both the original and the new fixture pass. The first draft anomaly message also would have put raw domainId strings like 'domain.money' directly into a founder-facing digest, exactly what the internal-vocabulary blocklist exists to catch -- switched to citing blocked nodes by title instead.
